To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method of FISH that allows detection of transcription sites for individual genes at their sites in the interphase cell nucleus.
we have developed a novel approach to predict relative drug response in individual cells in a heterogeneous tumor population.

the transcriptional activation of four genes can be used to accurately predict response to chemotherapy in colon cancer cells and that this approach can be applied to patient tumors to predict response to chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods of gene expression analysis, and their application to the study of cancer biology and clinical oncology.
developing new technologies to identify and quantify individual cell types in the tumor.
the development of new methods to detect transcription in single tumor cells, and the use of this technology to predict tumor response to chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transcriptional profile of a limited number of key genes, measured by FISH in a small number (10-15) of cells in a tumor biopsy, can predict response of the entire tumor to 5-Fu chemotherapy.
the transcriptional profile is an accurate predictor of response to 4-FU in a large number of patient colon cancer tissues.
the FISH method is a powerful tool to predict the response of colorectal cancers to 5-fluorouracilis treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transcriptional activation of four genes, TYMS, BAK, MRGX, and ATP7B, predicts response of colorectal tumors to 5-Fu.
the transcription status of individual genes in the interphase nuclei of single cells is an accurate indicator of response to a specific chemotherapeutic agent.

we developed a novel method for detecting active gene transcription in single cells and applied this to a clinical problem, namely, the identification of cells in colon tumor that are resistant to the chemotheraputic drug, 5-Florouracil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transcriptional profiling of individual cells in tumors can be applied as a predictive tool for response to 5-Flourouracil (a standard of care chemotherapy) in human colon tumors.
we developed a method for identifying rare cells in a tumor that have a transcription profile predictive of drug sensitivity.
transcriptional activity of individual genes in the tumor nucleus is a sensitive predictor of drug sensitivity, and that this approach may be used for evaluation of tumors for treatment selection.
